utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D448, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 1D1900.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, do you agree that the self-criticism of the state organs was sometimes so extreme as to be on the verge of masochism or mutual recriminations? Was this kind of responsibility or this kind of impotence because of the existing infrastructure, a feeling of impotence, was it something that led to these extreme cases of self-criticism?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that at government sessions there was criticism, self-criticism, co-ordination of opinions, and everything else which normally attends to the work of any state institution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is a letter by the minister of the interior --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we have the translation for this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, you have the B/C/S version before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a letter by the minister of the interior to the president -- to the prime minister, and can you tell us what the first paragraph is about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanisic is writing to the prime minister, Branko Djeric: "Mr. Prime Minister, although as a member of the government, I don't know how many times I've requested at sessions for a proposal of a law or a similar enactment to be endorsed which would, in keeping with International Law and International Law of War, channel the war activities of the army, of groups and individuals, in order for those not to be at variance with the sanctioned provisions of International Law, and the consequences of which could resemble genocide or war crimes, unfortunately, you have not done so to this very day, although I do believe that this topic should have been on the agenda of the first next governmental session."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you look further down. The whole page is, of course, interesting, but we do not have the time.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Precisely for the reason to disprove the existence of sanctioned intentions and actions, at your proposal or initiative, a platform or another document would have to be established from which it would stem a clear and civilised option in order to put into practice what I believe are certainly correct political objectives of the Serbian people, whereas, at the same time, with the text of the platform or another document, we should disassociate ourselves from all groups or individuals who would have different intentions, whereby we would confirm that, as a people, we should not be characterised with the epithet of a genocidal or criminal nation."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then he goes on to say: "I have to tell the prime minister that you did not work very much towards the establishment of military courts," and so on and so forth, "which has not been done to this very day, and that is why we have so many perpetrators of criminal offences of different ilk, and these are people who are not covered by the army and are also beyond the responsibility of the civilian institutions." Can you do this: "We are working on collecting ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only have the first page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the second page, the following page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The underlined parts.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We are working on collecting and documenting the criminal -- the crimes of -- the criminal offence of war crimes, i.e., genocide, irrespective of who the perpetrators are and what their ethnicity is."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "By letter, I shall inform you personally, the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as the federal -- SUP of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, attached to which is working a commission where we also have one of our members, of precisely the foregoing issues." Signed by Mico Stanisic, the 18th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this already a well-advanced stage of the conflict between Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Djeric?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a personal conflict. This is a struggle of opinions and a confrontation of position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, the fact that your professors are actually translating this to the personal plane, is that -- that is another thing. Are you saying that I actually favour the professors in the government?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D449, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll rise for today, Mr. Karadzic. Tomorrow, we are sitting -- we are beginning at -- Mr. Mandic, do you have something to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask you, Your Honour: How many more hours will I be here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You'll be done on Friday. I hope that the Trial Chamber will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By the end of today, Mr. Karadzic has had 16 hours and 15 minutes, which means he will have at least 3 hours and 45 minutes in order to conclude his cross-examination in 20 hours, which was originally allowed by the Trial Chamber. He's requesting some further time, and then the Chamber will consider. So tomorrow we'll be sitting in a slightly extended form, but in total -- in average, the time for evidence is usually around four hours and something, a bit less than that, so it seems inevitable you may need to stay on Friday. I can't say for sure how long we will need on Friday. We'll decide by the end of tomorrow's session. There's one thing: Tomorrow, we originally planned to sit from 9.00 to 3.00, but given that at least two members of the Bench are sitting in other cases, so although there may be not any sitting trial, it's better to conclude as early as possible. And the Chamber inquired of the Registry people whether it would be feasible to sit from 9.00 to 2.30, having only two half-an-hour breaks, and we received the positive answers. So unless the parties object to that kind of scheduling, we'll sit in that way: 9.00 to 2.30, two 30 minutes' break. Thank you. Have a nice evening. I'll see you at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of July, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.07 p.m.,
